fetched.title: ClickUp's MCP Server
fetched.text:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a secure, standardized framework that lets external AI agents interact with ClickUp Workspace data—like tasks, lists, folders, and docs—using natural language. MCP helps users, especially developers, automate workflows, connect third-party AI tools, and enable agentic AI features in their preferred apps, all while keeping security and user control tight.

ClickUp's MCP Server is available on all plans.

# Setup instructions

Learn how to setup your AI assistant with ClickUp's MCP server.

Our MCP server URL is `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`.

# What you can do

With ClickUp's MCP server, you can:

* **Orchestrate task workflows**: Manage tasks with assignees, priorities, and due dates across lists and spaces.
* **Build executive reports**: Create release notes, status updates, and portfolio summaries from tasks and docs.
* **Track time**: Log time entries and manage timers.
* **Answer work questions**: Search tasks, docs, and comments for quick answers.
* **Collaborate in comments and chat**: Summarize threads, extract action items, and post updates. And more!

# Supported MCP Clients

ClickUp MCP supports all major MCP clients and Apps.

# Supported tools

Learn about the tools available through ClickUp's MCP Server with example prompts you can use in your AI assistant.

# Rate limits

ClickUp's MCP Server has rate limits that depend on two criteria:

1. If your Workspace has purchased the Everything AI add-on.
2. Your Workspace plan.

> 📘
>
> **Note:**
>
> * MCP usage and rate limits are subject to the terms of our fair use policy.
> * Future restrictions may apply to ClickUp MCP features.
> * ClickUp MCP usage and rate limits may change as we assess usage and costs.

## With the Everything AI add-on

If your Workspace has purchased the Everything AI add-on, your MCP rate limits are the same as the rate limits for our Public API, which vary by plan.

## Without the Everything AI add-on

If your Workspace has not purchased the Everything AI add-on, your MCP usage is subject to the following rate limits by plan:

| Plan | MCP Calls per rolling 24 hours |
| --- | --- |
| Free Forever | 100 |
| Core/Unlimited | 300 |
| Business | 1,000 |
| Business Plus | 2,500 |
| Enterprise | 5,000 |
| Enterprise Plus | 25,000 |

  

### Rolling 24-hour rate limits

* **Limits are per Workspace and per client.** Example: an Unlimited Workspace gets 300/24h for Claude and a separate 300/24h for Cursor.
* Each tool call counts as 1. `initialize` and `tools/list` don't count. When the limit is hit, the call returns `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `retryAfter`.
* Plans with no daily cap still follow the public API per-minute limits, and MCP shares that budget with the public API.
* MCP doesn't use AI Super Credits.

  The rolling 24-hour rate limits begin with your first request.

  + For example, starting on Monday at 1 pm, you use the MCP to send 200 requests.
  + On Tuesday, at 11 am, you send another 100 requests.
  + You will be rate-limited and unable to send additional requests via MCP until 1 pm on Tuesday.
* Attempting to send requests while rate limited does not extend the 24 hour limit.
* Rate limits cannot be reset.

# FAQ

**Q. Can I authenticate with my own API keys or Auth access tokens?**

**A.** No, you cannot authenticate using your own API keys or Auth access tokens. We only support OAuth for authentication.

  

**Q. Why can't I delete things with the MCP?**

**A.** For the time being, we haven’t added any deletion tools as a safety measure. Feel free to leave your feedback here.

  

**Q. Can I search my apps with Connected Search using ClickUp MCP?**

**A.** No, it is not possible to search connected apps.

  

**Q. Can I connect my custom LLM Client?**

**A.** Yes, if your team builds an MCP client implementation that meets the following criteria:

* Implements the JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over HTTP.
* Supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE authentication.
* Follows the MCP specification.

Updated about 2 months ago

---

fetched.title: Supported Tools
fetched.text:
The ClickUp MCP exposes many of the capabilities available in our API. The real magic happens when your AI assistant combines several tools to complete a larger request.

***Note:** Your AI assistant will only be able to perform actions in ClickUp that you have permission to do.*

# Search

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search Workspace | Searches for items across the entire ClickUp Workspace, including tasks, Docs, dashboards, attachments, whiteboards, Chats, and forms. | "Find all tasks related to the 'Q4 Marketing Launch'." |
| Search tasks by tag | Retrieves tasks filtered by tags. | "Show me the tasks with the 'UX-quality' tag." |

# Task management

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Task | Creates a new task in a specific List. You can specify details like the task name, description, assignees, due date, and priority. | "Create a task to 'Draft blog post' in the 'Content Pipeline' List, assign it to me, and set the due date for this Friday." |
| Get Task | Retrieves the full details of a single task using its unique task ID. | "What are the details for task 'Design-123'?" |
| Update Task | Modifies the properties of an existing task. This can include changing the task's name, description, status, assignees, or due date. | "Change the status of task 'Draft blog post' to 'In Progress' and add 'Review' as a subtask." |
| Set Custom Fields | Set Custom Fields on tasks. ***Note:*** *Your AI assistant understands the Custom Fields, options, and supported values that are available on tasks.* | "Set the 'release number' to '4.07'." |
| Get Custom Fields | Retrieves the Custom Fields available on a List, Folder, Space, or Workspace. | "What Custom Fields does the 'Bugs' List have?" |
| Delete task | Deletes a task or subtask. ***Note:*** *Your AI assistant may confirm the correct task is selected before deleting the task.* | "Delete the "testing use only" task." |
| Merge tasks | Merges one or more tasks into a target task, combining their comments, attachments, subtasks, and tracked time. | "Merge the duplicate 'Login bug' tasks into the original one." |

## Manage tasks in bulk

Bulk actions run through the **Execute Operator** tool (see Generic operations).

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create tasks in bulk (`clickup_execute_operator`, `task.create_many`) | Creates multiple tasks in a specified List with a single call. | "Add these items as new tasks in the 'Onboarding' List: 'Send welcome email', 'Schedule orientation', and 'Set up hardware'." |
| Update tasks in bulk (`clickup_execute_operator`, `task.update_many`) | Applies the same change to multiple tasks at once. This is useful for changing the status, assignee, or due date for a group of tasks simultaneously. | "Move all tasks in the 'Sprint 3' List with the 'Ready for Review' status to 'In Review'." |

## Task attachments

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attach File to Task | Uploads and attaches a file (like a document, image, or ZIP file) to a specific task. | "Attach this document [file\_upload] to the 'Submit Final Report' task." |
| Request Attachment Upload | Gets a short-lived upload link for adding a large file (up to 1 GB) to a task or Chat. | "Upload this recording to the 'Customer Interview' task." |
| Download Task Attachment | Retrieves a file attached to a task. | "Open the spec PDF attached to task 'Design-123'." |

## Task comments

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Task Comments | Retrieves all comments from a specific task. | "What's the latest update on the 'Develop new feature' task?" |
| Get Threaded Replies | Retrieves threaded replies under a parent task comment. | "Summarize this comment thread and tell me my action items." |
| Create Task Comment | Adds a new comment to a task. This can be used to ask questions, provide updates, or @mention other team members. | "Add a comment to task 'Design-123' saying: '@Mark, can you please provide the latest mockups?'" |
| Create Comment | Adds a comment to a task, List, or view, or replies to an existing comment. | "Reply to Mark's comment and say the mockups are attached." |
| Update Comment | Edits, resolves, or reassigns an existing comment. | "Resolve my comment on the 'Design-123' task." |
| Delete Comment | Deletes a comment. | "Delete my last comment on the 'Design-123' task." |

## Task tags

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Space Tag | Creates a new tag that every task in a Space can use. | "Create an 'Urgent' tag in the 'Engineering' Space." |
| Add Tag to Task | Applies an existing tag (label) to a task for categorization. | "Add the 'Urgent' tag to task 'Fix login bug'." |
| Remove Tag from Task | Removes a specific tag from a task. | "Remove the 'Backend' tag from task 'Update button color'." |

## Task relationships

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add task link | Relate two tasks by linking them. | "Link feature 123 with design for feature 123." |
| Remove task link | Remove links between tasks. | "Remove the link between feature 123 and scope designs for feature 123." |
| Add dependency | Create a dependency relationship between tasks. | "This task is blocked by its subtask called 'support Google authentication'." |
| Remove dependency | Remove a dependency relationship between tasks. | "Remove the dependency between feature 123 and support Google authentication." |

## Move and add tasks to other Lists

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move task to a new List | Move a task to a new home List. | "Move the feature 123 task from the Backlog List to 'Sprint 3'." |
| Add task to another List | Add a task to another List. | "Add the feature 123 task to 'Sprint 3'." |
| Remove task from a List | Remove a task from an additional List. The task stays in its home List. | "Take the feature 123 task out of 'Sprint 3'." |

# Time tracking

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Task Time Entries | Retrieves all time log entries for a specific task. | "How much time has been logged for the 'Client Research' task?" |
| Get time entries for multiple tasks | Retrieves time entries and totals across tasks, filtered by date range, assignee, or billable status. | "How much time did I log last week?" |
| Start Time Tracking | Starts a timer for a specific task for the current user. | "Start tracking time for the 'Code Review' task." |
| Stop Time Tracking | Stops the currently active timer for the user. | "Stop the timer." |
| Add Time Entry | Manually adds a block of time (a time entry) to a task, including a start and end time or a duration. | "Log 2 hours of work on the 'Database optimization' task for yesterday." |
| Get Current Time Entry | Checks if the user has a timer currently running and, if so, returns the details of that time entry. | "What am I currently tracking time for?" |

# Workspace Hierarchy

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Workspace Hierarchy | Retrieves the full structure of the Workspace, including all Spaces, Folders, and Lists. | "Show me all the Lists in the 'Engineering' Space." |
| Create List | Creates a new List within a specific Space. To create a List inside a Folder, use Create List in Folder. | "Create a new List named 'Sprint 4 Planning' in the 'Product' Space." |
| Create List in Folder | Creates a new List specifically inside a designated Folder. | "Inside the 'Marketing Campaigns' Folder, create a new List called 'Social Media Content'." |
| Get List | Retrieves the details and settings for a single List. | "What are the custom statuses for the 'Bugs' List?" |
| Update List | Modifies the settings of an existing List, such as changing its name, description, or status. | "Rename the 'New Ideas' List to 'Approved Ideas'." |
| Get Folder | Retrieves the details for a single Folder, such as its ID, name, and the Space it belongs to. | "Which Space is the 'Client Projects' Folder in?" |
| Create Folder | Creates a new Folder within a specific Space. | "Create a new Folder named 'Q1 Projects' in the 'Operations' Space." |
| Update Folder | Modifies the settings of an existing Folder, such as changing its name. | "Rename the 'Design' Folder to 'Design Team'." |

# Members and assignees

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Workspace Members | Retrieves a list of all members and guests in the Workspace. | "Who are all the members of this Workspace?" |
| Find Member by Name | Searches for a Workspace member using their name or email. | "What is David Smith's user ID?" |
| Resolve Assignees | A utility to confirm and retrieve the user objects for a list of potential assignees, often used before adding them to a task. | "When you say, 'Assign this task to Mark and Sarah,' this tool finds the correct user IDs for 'Mark' and 'Sarah'." |
| Get User | Retrieves the signed-in user, their timezone, and the current time. | "What time is it for me right now?" |

# Chat

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Chat Channels | Retrieves a list of all Chat channels (views) in the Workspace. | "List all available Chat channels." |
| Send Chat Message | Sends a message to a specific Chat channel. | "Post a message in the 'General' channel: 'Team lunch at 1 PM today.'" |
| Get Channel Messages | Retrieves recent messages from a Chat channel. | "What did I miss in the 'General' channel today?" |
| Get Message Replies | Retrieves the replies in a message thread. | "Summarize the replies to the launch announcement." |
| Update Chat Message | Edits, resolves, or reassigns a message. | "Fix the typo in my last message in 'General'." |
| React to Chat Message | Adds or removes your emoji reaction on a message. | "Give the launch announcement a 🎉." |

# Docs

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Document | Creates a new Doc within the Workspace, usually in a specific location (like a Space or Folder) or in the private Docs area. | "Create a new document named 'Project Kickoff Notes' in the 'Project Phoenix' Space." |
| List Document Pages | Retrieves the structure or table of contents of a Doc, listing all its pages. | "What are the pages in the 'Employee Handbook' Doc?" |
| Get Document Pages | Retrieves the content of one or more pages from a specific Doc. | "Show me the content of the 'Onboarding' page from the 'Team Wiki' Doc." |
| Create Document Page | Adds a new page (or sub-page) to an existing Doc. | "Add a new page titled 'Security Protocols' to the 'Company Policies' Doc." |
| Update Document Page | Edits the content of an existing page within a Doc. | "On the 'Security Protocols' page, add a new section for 'Password Management'." |
| List Page Attachments | Lists the files attached to a Doc page. | "What files are attached to the 'Onboarding' page?" |
| Download Page Attachment | Retrieves a file attached to a Doc page. | "Open the org chart attached to the 'Onboarding' page." |

# Time in status reporting

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Time in Status for a task | Retrieve the amount of time a task has been in a status. | "How long has feature 123 been in progress?" |
| Get Time in Status for multiple tasks | Retrieve time in status metrics for up to 100 tasks by task ID. | "How long did these five tasks spend in QA review?" |

# Reminders

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Reminder | Creates a personal reminder. | "Remind me to send the report Friday at 9 AM." |
| Update Reminder | Edits or completes one of your reminders. | "Move my report reminder to Monday." |
| Search Reminders | Finds your reminders. | "What reminders do I have this week?" |

# Generic operations

| Tool | Definition | Example usage (for an AI assistant) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get Operators | Lists the extra operations this server allows, such as bulk task changes, archiving, statuses, views, and forms. | "Can you archive tasks?" |
| Get Schema | Describes how ClickUp objects relate to each other. | (Used by your AI assistant to plan requests.) |
| Execute Operator | Runs one of those operations, such as creating or updating tasks in bulk. | "Archive the three 'old campaign' tasks." |

# Tool details

To connect a client and sign in, see MCP Server Setup Instructions. Tool names below are the exact names your MCP client sees.

Every tool acts as the signed-in user, with that user's ClickUp permissions, exactly as in the app. The server adds no access of its own. In ChatGPT Team, Enterprise and Edu workspaces, only owners and admins can configure MCP servers. Every tool also accepts an optional `workspace_id` (required when the user belongs to more than one workspace; if it's missing, the server lists the choices).

**Columns:** **Type** is Read or Write. **Sensitive** marks tools that delete or irreversibly overwrite data, post content as the user, or move files. **Side effects** covers what changes in ClickUp and who is notified.

## Tasks

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_create_task` | Write | No | `name`, `list_id`. Optional: status, priority, dates, assignees (user IDs), watchers, tags, custom fields, parent, time estimate, task type | Task ID and URL | Creates a task. Assignees and watchers are notified. Missing tags are created. Repeating the call creates a duplicate. |
| `clickup_get_task` | Read | No | `task_id`. Optional: `include`, `expand_statuses` | Task summary, plus valid statuses when requested | None |
| `clickup_update_task` | Write | No | `task_id` plus fields to change | Task ID and URL | Overwrites the given fields. Setting assignees replaces the whole list. Affected people are notified. Each field needs its own permission (e.g. Change Status). |
| `clickup_delete_task` | Write | **Yes** | `task_id` | Task ID | Sends the task and its subtasks to Trash. Requires Delete permission. |
| `clickup_filter_tasks` | Read | No | All optional: lists, folders, spaces, statuses, assignees, tags, dates, custom fields, or `view_id` | Tasks, paged | None |
| `clickup_move_task` | Write | No | `task_id`, destination `list_id` | New List ID | Moves the task. Its current status must exist in the destination List. |
| `clickup_add_task_to_list` | Write | No | `task_id`, `list_id` | Success | Task also appears in a second List. Requires the Tasks in Multiple Lists ClickApp. |
| `clickup_remove_task_from_list` | Write | No | `task_id`, `list_id` | Success | Removes the task from an extra List. The task itself remains. |
| `clickup_merge_tasks` | Write | **Yes** | Target `task_id`, `source_task_ids` | Merged task ID | Moves assignees, comments, attachments, subtasks and tracked time into the target and consumes the sources. No undo. Requires Merge permission on every task. |

**Bulk create / update:** use `clickup_execute_operator` with `task.create_many` or `task.update_many` (see Generic operations).

## Task relationships and tags

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_add_task_dependency` | Write | No | `task_id`, `depends_on`, `type` (waiting on / blocking) | Success | Adds a dependency, shown on both tasks. |
| `clickup_remove_task_dependency` | Write | No | `task_id`, `depends_on`, `type` | Success | Removes the dependency. |
| `clickup_add_task_link` | Write | No | `task_id`, `links_to` | Success | Links two tasks. |
| `clickup_remove_task_link` | Write | No | `task_id`, `links_to` | Success | Removes the link. |
| `clickup_create_space_tag` | Write | No | `space_id`, `name`. Optional: colors | Tag, and whether it was new | Creates a Space-wide tag. No-op if it exists. |
| `clickup_add_tag_to_task` | Write | No | `task_id`, `tag_name` (must exist) | Success | Tags the task. |
| `clickup_remove_tag_from_task` | Write | No | `task_id`, `tag_name` | Success | Untags the task. The tag stays in the Space. |
| `clickup_get_custom_fields` | Read | No | One or more of `list_id`, `folder_id`, `space_id`, `include_workspace` | Field definitions per level | None |

## Time tracking

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_start_time_tracking` | Write | No | `task_id`. Optional: description, billable, tags | Running entry | Starts the user's timer. Refuses if one is already running. |
| `clickup_stop_time_tracking` | Write | No | All optional: description, tags, `time_entry_id` | Finished entry | Stops the timer and saves the entry. |
| `clickup_add_time_entry` | Write | No | `task_id`, `start`, and `duration` or `end_time` | New entry | Logs time. Repeating the call counts the time twice. |
| `clickup_get_current_time_entry` | Read | No | None | Running entry, if any | None |
| `clickup_get_time_entries` | Read | No | All optional: `task_id`, dates, `assignee`, billable | Entries and totals | None. Other people's time appears only if the user can see it. |
| `clickup_get_task_time_in_status` | Read | No | `task_id` | Time in each status | None. Requires the Total time in Status ClickApp. |
| `clickup_get_bulk_tasks_time_in_status` | Read | No | `task_ids` (up to 100) | Time in each status, per task | None. Same ClickApp required. |

## Attachments

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_attach_task_file` | Write | **Yes** | `task_id`, plus base64 `file_data` or `file_url` | Attachment ID and URL | Adds a file visible to everyone on the task. URLs are fetched by the server (up to 100 MB). |
| `clickup_request_attachment_upload` | Write | **Yes** | Exactly one of `task_id`, `channel_id`, `parent_message_id` | Short-lived upload URL and ticket | None by itself. The client then uploads a file (up to 1 GB) to the task or chat. |
| `clickup_download_task_attachment` | Read | No | `task_id`, `attachment_id` | File details and a ~5 minute download link | None |

## Comments

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_create_comment` | Write | **Yes** | `comment_text`, plus `entity_id` (task, List or view) or `reply_to_id`. Optional: `notify_all`, `assignee` | Comment ID | Posts as the user. Mentioned people (or all assignees with `notify_all`) are notified. |
| `clickup_create_task_comment` | Write | **Yes** | `task_id`, `comment_text` | Comment ID | Same as `clickup_create_comment` (legacy name). |
| `clickup_get_task_comments` | Read | No | `task_id`. Optional: paging | Comments with reply counts | None |
| `clickup_get_threaded_comments` | Read | No | `comment_id` | Replies | None |
| `clickup_update_comment` | Write | **Yes** | `comment_id`, plus new text, `resolved` or `assignee` | Comment ID | Replaces the text, or resolves/reassigns the comment. |
| `clickup_delete_comment` | Write | **Yes** | `comment_id` | Comment ID | Deletes the comment. Cannot be undone by the tool. |

## Docs

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_create_document` | Write | No | `name`, `parent`, `visibility`, `create_page` | Doc ID and URL | Creates a Doc. `PUBLIC` means visible to members who can open the parent, not the internet. |
| `clickup_list_document_pages` | Read | No | `document_id` | Page names and structure | None |
| `clickup_get_document_pages` | Read | No | `document_id`, `page_ids` | Page content (plain text or Markdown) | None |
| `clickup_create_document_page` | Write | No | `document_id`, `name`, `content` | Page ID | Adds a page. |
| `clickup_update_document_page` | Write | **Yes** | `document_id`, `page_id`. Optional: content, title, `content_edit_mode` | Page ID | Replaces the whole page by default. `append` / `prepend` keep existing content. |
| `clickup_list_document_page_attachments` | Read | No | `page_id` | File details, paged | None |
| `clickup_download_document_page_attachment` | Read | No | `page_id`, `attachment_id` | ~5 minute download link | None |

## Chat

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_get_chat_channels` | Read | No | Optional paging | Channels | None |
| `clickup_get_chat_channel_messages` | Read | No | `channel_id`. Optional: paging, reactions | Messages | None |
| `clickup_get_chat_message_replies` | Read | No | `message_id` | Thread replies | None |
| `clickup_send_chat_message` | Write | **Yes** | `content`, plus one of `channel_id`, `user_ids` (DM, up to 15 people), `parent_message_id` | Message ID | Posts as the user. Channel members or recipients see it and are notified. |
| `clickup_update_chat_message` | Write | **Yes** | `message_id`, plus content, title, resolved or assignee | Message ID | Replaces the message text. Files omitted from the new text are removed. |
| `clickup_react_to_chat_message` | Write | No | `message_id`, `add` or `remove`, emoji | Success | Adds or removes the user's own reaction. |

## Lists and Folders

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_get_list` | Read | No | `list_id` or `list_name` | List details, including its statuses | None |
| `clickup_create_list` | Write | No | `name`, plus `space_id` or `space_name` | List ID and URL | Creates a List in a Space. |
| `clickup_create_list_in_folder` | Write | No | `name`, `folder_id` | List ID and URL | Creates a List in a Folder. |
| `clickup_update_list` | Write | No | `list_id`, plus name, description or status | Success | Overwrites those fields. |
| `clickup_get_folder` | Read | No | `folder_id`, or Folder name plus Space | Folder details | None |
| `clickup_create_folder` | Write | No | `name`, plus `space_id` or `space_name` | Folder ID | Creates a Folder. |
| `clickup_update_folder` | Write | No | `folder_id`, plus name or `override_statuses` | Success | Renames the Folder, or changes statuses for every List in it. |

## Reminders (the user's own)

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_create_reminder` | Write | No | `title`, `due_date`. Optional: description | Reminder | Creates a personal reminder. |
| `clickup_update_reminder` | Write | No | `reminder_id`, plus fields to change | Reminder | Edits or completes the user's own reminder. |
| `clickup_search_reminders` | Read | No | Optional filters and paging | Reminders | None |

## Workspace, people and search

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_get_workspace_hierarchy` | Read | No | Optional depth, Space IDs, paging | Spaces, Folders and Lists the user can see | None |
| `clickup_get_workspace_members` | Read | No | None | Members, including email addresses | None |
| `clickup_find_member_by_name` | Read | No | `name_or_email` | One member | None |
| `clickup_resolve_assignees` | Read | No | Names, emails or "me" | User IDs | None |
| `clickup_get_user` | Read | No | None | Signed-in user, timezone, current time | None |
| `clickup_search` | Read | No | All optional: keywords, filters, sort, paging | Matching tasks, Docs, chats and more | None |

## Generic operations (Unified API)

| Tool | Type | Sensitive | Inputs | Returns | Side effects / permissions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clickup_get_operators` | Read | No | Optional filter | Allowed operations and their inputs | None |
| `clickup_get_schema` | Read | No | Optional filter | How ClickUp objects relate | None |
| `clickup_execute_operator` | Write | **Yes** | `model`, `operator`. Optional: parameters, body, query | The operation's result | Runs one allowed operation as the user. Don't retry a timeout; the operation may have completed. |

Allowed operations: **Tasks:** read many by ID, create many (`task.create_many`), update many (`task.update_many`, one shared change applied to every named task), archive, unarchive. **Lists and statuses:** update a List; read statuses of a List, Space or Folder; add, rename or remove a Space's statuses. **Custom fields:** create, list. **Views:** create, update, read, list. **Forms:** create, update, read, list. None of these delete anything; archive is reversible. Bulk update and archive must name task IDs.

# Status handling

* **Success:** a normal result. Writes return `success: true` plus the IDs of what changed.
* **Failure:** a result with `isError: true` and a JSON body `{"error": "..."}` (see Errors).
* **No pending states:** every tool completes in a single request; there is nothing to poll.
* **Paging:** pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. Cursor-paged read tools also return `has_more`.
* **Partial results:** some writes return `warnings` naming parts of the request that weren't applied (e.g. an unresolvable watcher) while the rest succeeded.
* **Task statuses:** statuses are defined per List. Use `clickup_get_list` or `clickup_get_task` (with `expand_statuses`) to find a List's valid statuses before setting one.

# Errors

| Error | Meaning | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... error="invalid_token"` | Sign-in missing or invalid | Sign in again |
| HTTP 400 | `x-workspace-id` header isn't a number | Fix the header |
| HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60` | Too many requests to the server | Wait, then retry |
| JSON-RPC `-32602` `Unknown tool: <name>` | Tool doesn't exist or is switched off | No |
| Tool result `isError: true`, `{"error":"Failed to <action>: <reason>"}` | The operation failed | See below |
| Tool result `errorCode: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `retryAfter: <seconds>` | Daily or per-plan limit reached | Retry after `retryAfter` seconds |

* Bad input, permission or "not found" errors: don't retry; change the request.
* "Request timed out" or "ClickUp server error" on a **read**: safe to retry.
* Same errors on a **write**: check whether it happened first. Creates, sends, comments and time entries make a second copy if repeated.

# Rate limits

* **Server:** 1,000 requests per minute per connection.
* **File uploads:** 20 per 15 minutes per user, up to 1 GB per file.
* **Daily MCP call limits by plan:** see ClickUp's MCP Server.

# Setup instructions

Below are the setup instructions for some of the most popular AI assistants.

## Claude

Set up Claude to use the ClickUp MCP server!

### Pro, Team, Enterprise

If you're on the Pro, Team, or Enterprise plan:

1. In a browser or the desktop app, navigate to Settings in the sidebar.
2. Scroll to Connectors at the bottom and click Add.
3. In the prompt, enter the following:

* Name: ClickUp
* Remote MCP Server URL: https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp

### Free

If you're on the Free plan of Claude, you'll set up the MCP server from the Claude desktop app:

1. Go to your Claude desktop settings page.
2. Click on Developer section.
3. Click on edit config then open the `claude_desktop_config.json` with your editor of choice.
4. Add the following and restart the Claude desktop app:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clickup": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

Use the follow command: `claude mcp add --transport http clickup https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`

Once you've opened a Claude Code session, run /mcp to go through the authentication flow.

## Cursor

Install here, or from Cursor's MCP directory page.

### Manual installation

To manually set up Cursor for the ClickUp MCP server, add the following to your mcp.json file:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clickup": {
      "url": "https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Devin

Set up Devin to use the ClickUp MCP Server.

### Manual installation

1. Open your **Devin settings**.
2. Navigate to the **MCP Marketplace**.
3. Click the button to **Add your own MCP**.
4. Enter a name for the server (e.g., "ClickUp").
5. Set the **Transport Type** to **HTTP**.
6. Enter a short description.
7. Paste the following link into the **Server URL** field: https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp
8. For Authentication, select **OAuth**.
9. Enable the server.

The first time you use the integration, Devin will attempt to connect and ask for authorization. Click the link provided to authorize your ClickUp workspace.

## Microsoft Copilot Studio

Set up Microsoft Copilot Studio to use the ClickUp MCP Server.

### Manual installation

1. Open Microsoft Copilot Studio and navigate to your Agent.
2. Scroll down to the **Tools** section.
3. Click **Add Tool**.
4. Then click **New tool**
5. Select **Model Context Protocol**.
6. Enter a Name for the tool, such as `ClickUp`
7. Enter a short Description for the tool.
8. Paste the Server URL: https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp
9. For Authentication, select **OAuth**.
10. Ensure the configuration is set to **Dynamic Discovery (DCR)**.
11. Click **Create** to finish setting up the tool.

## VS Code

Set up VS Code to use the ClickUp MCP server!

### Manual installation

To manually set up VS Code for the ClickUp MCP server, open a terminal and run the following command:

`code --add-mcp '{"type":"http","name":"clickup","url":"https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp"}'`

Then, from inside VS Code, go to your extensions section.

You will find ClickUp MCP at the bottom of the list of MCP servers.

Click the settings **cogwheel** on the ClickUp MCP and click **Start Server**.

Follow the links to finish the authentication flow.

## Windsurf

To set up Windsurf for the ClickUp MCP server:

1. Press Ctrl + , on Windows or Cmd + , on Mac to open your Windsurf settings.
2. Under Scroll to Cascade, click MCP servers.
3. Click Add Server, then select Add custom server.
4. Copy the following JSON to your Windsurf MCP config file:

   ```
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "clickup": {
         "serverUrl": "https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

## ChatGPT

> 🔓
>
> **Note**: In Team, Enterprise, and Edu workspaces, only owners and admins have permission to configure MCP servers.

Use the ClickUp MCP app in ChatGPT. Learn more

To connect the ClickUp app from ChatGPT:

1. Navigate to **Apps**.
2. Search for **ClickUp**, or browse the **Productivity** category.
3. Select ClickUp, then click **Connect**.
4. Click **Connect ClickUp**.
5. Sign into your ClickUp account, and select the Workspace(s) you want to use with ChatGPT.

   > 🔁
   >
   > **Note**: You can update the available Workspaces or ClickUp account you want to use at any time by reconnecting the app.
6. Click **Connect Workspace**.
7. Click **Start Chat** to use ClickUp with ChatGPT.

### Reconnect or disconnect ClickUp in ChatGPT

To reconnect or disconnect ClickUp and ChatGPT:

1. From Apps, search or browse for the ClickUp app.
2. Click the **settings cog** icon.
3. Click the **ellipsis** icon, then **Reconnect** to reconnect ClickUp and ChatGPT.
4. Click **Disconnect** to remove the app.

## Antigravity

To set up Antigravity to use the ClickUp MCP Server, you can review the Antigravity Docs from Google here .

Following the instructions under **Connecting Custom MCP Servers**, add the following to your `mcp_config.json` file:

```
{
    "mcpServers": {
        "clickup": {
            "serverUrl": "https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp"
        }
    }
}
```

## Other clients

You can configure most other clients to use ClickUp's MCP server with the following settings:

```
Command: npx
Arguments: -y mcp-remote https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp 
Environment: None
```

fetched.title: What is ClickUp MCP?
fetched.text:
## Search

Ask me anything

Your AI models and agents can use our official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to access your ClickUp data in a simple and secure way. It's designed to work seamlessly with popular AI assistants like ChatGPT, Cursor, and Claude.

ClickUp MCP is available on all plans.  
  
You can set up the ClickUp MCP server with any app that supports MCP servers, like Claude, Cursor, or VS Code.

Workspaces are being upgraded to our new plans. Not all Workspaces have been upgraded yet. Learn more

# What can I do with the ClickUp MCP server?

* **Orchestrate task workflows**: Create, enrich, and route tasks with assignees, Priorities, and due dates across Lists and Spaces.
* **Build executive reports**: Produce release notes, status updates, and portfolio rollups consolidated from tasks, comments, and Docs.
* **Track time**: Start and stop timers, log historical entries, and fetch entries.
* **Answer questions from work**: Search tasks, Docs, and comments to deliver quick, context-rich answers.
* **Collaborate in comments and Chat**: Summarize threads, extract action items, and post updates. Attach files and images to Channel messages, Posts, and Channel thread replies.

# Available tools

ClickUp's MCP server enables AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or VS Code, to integrate with ClickUp's tools and data. This means your AI assistant can now execute actions, retrieve information, and provide intelligent, context-aware insights instantly.

For a full list of supported tools, read this developer article.

Before you connect an MCP client, review the rate limits section below to learn which rate limits apply to your Workspace and how usage is counted.

# Example requests

Below are some examples of requests you could make after you've connected your AI assistant to ClickUp's MCP server:

* `Create a task for this bug we're working on.`
* `Find all my incomplete tasks due this week.`
* `List all milestones in the Product Launch project.`
* `How many hours has the team spent on clients this month?`

# Setup instructions

For step-by-step setup instructions, read our MCP Server Setup Instructions article.

# Rate limits

ClickUp's MCP Server has rate limits that depend on two criteria:

1. If your Workspace has purchased the Everything AI add-on.
2. Your Workspace plan.

MCP rate limits and public API rate limits are two separate limits. The public API limits requests per minute, per token. Without the Everything AI add-on, ClickUp MCP limits calls per rolling 24-hour period instead.

## With the Everything AI add-on

If your Workspace has purchased the Everything AI add-on, your MCP rate limits are the same as the rate limits for our Public API which vary by plan.

On our new plans that include ClickUp AI, AI is included with your plan instead of as separate add-ons.

With the add-on, the rolling 24-hour limit no longer applies. Your MCP requests count toward the same per-minute, per-token limit as the public API:

* **Free Forever, Unlimited, and Business Plans**: 100 requests per minute, per token.
* **Business Plus Plan**: 1,000 requests per minute, per token.
* **Enterprise Plan**: 10,000 requests per minute, per token.

On our new plans that include ClickUp AI, daily MCP limits differ by plan.

## Without the Everything AI add-on

If your Workspace has not purchased the Everything AI add-on, your MCP usage is subject to the following daily rate limits by plan:

* **Free Forever Plan**: 100 calls per 24 hours.
* **Unlimited Plan**: 300 calls per 24 hours.
* **Business Plan**: 1,000 calls per 24 hours.
* **Business Plus Plan**: 2,500 calls per 24 hours.
* **Enterprise Plan**: 5,000 calls per 24 hours.

Each person has their own daily limit. All the MCP clients you connect, such as Claude and Cursor, share that limit.

Every MCP request counts toward the limit, including everyday actions like reading, creating, and updating tasks. It isn't limited to AI-generated actions.

## Rolling 24 hour rate limits

The rolling 24 hour rate limit begins with your first request.

For example, if your first MCP request on Monday is at 1pm and you reach your plan's daily limit by Tuesday at 11am, you will be rate limited until 1pm on Tuesday, 24 hours after your first request.

Attempting to send requests while rate limited does not extend the 24 hour window.

Rate limits cannot be reset.

When you reach the limit, MCP requests return a `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error until the rolling 24 hour window resets.

# FAQ

Frequently asked questions about the ClickUp MCP server.

### Can I monitor how many MCP calls my Workspace has used?

Not at this time.

### Can I authenticate with my own API keys or access tokens?

No, only OAuth is supported. OAuth is an industry-standard protocol that provides secure, delegated access. It lets you grant limited access to your resources without sharing credentials, supports granular permissions, and makes it easy to revoke access.

API keys are less secure because they’re static, usually have broad access, and are harder to manage or revoke if compromised.

### Can I use ClickUp MCP to search external apps I've connected to my ClickUp Workspace?

No, Connected Search can only be used from within your Workspace. For a list of all external apps that support Connected Search, read our Connected Search article.

### Do admins need to take any action inside ClickUp before setting up an external tool like Claude or ChatGPT?

No action is needed inside ClickUp. ClickUp MCP will provide the list of available tools.

### Will my custom LLM connect?

Yes, if your team builds an MCP client implementation that meets the following criteria:

* Implements the JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over HTTP
* Supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE authentication
* Follows the MCP specification

## Can't find what you're looking for?

Contact Us

fetched.title: Connect an MCP server to your Workspace
fetched.text:
## Search

Ask me anything

Integrate external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers like GitHub MCP or Atlassian MCP with your ClickUp Workspace, allowing your ClickUp Super Agents and ClickUp Brain to use tools from external apps.

For example, you can connect your CRM's MCP server to your Workspace. Your Super Agents and Brain can then use available MCP tools to take actions, such as creating CRM records, provisioning accounts, or syncing customer data, all from ClickUp.

For MCP call limits by plan, read ClickUp AI feature availability and limits.

This article covers connecting ClickUp to external MCP servers via the App Center (outbound connections). Connecting to the ClickUp MCP server, where an external AI client connects to your ClickUp data, is a separate feature governed by Personal API Token permissions.

You can connect an external MCP server on any plan.  
  
Only Workspace owners and admins can set up Workspace connections.  
  
Members can set up personal connections from the App Center if admins enable the Connect Personal MCP Server permission.  
  
Guests and limited members cannot set up integrations.  
  
Currently, you can only connect MCP servers from the ClickUp browser app.

# Connection types

When connecting an external MCP server, you'll select a connection type:

* **Just for me**: This is a personal connection. Connect your external MCP server account with your ClickUp user account for each Workspace you've created or joined. Only you will be able to use tools from this connection in Super Agents and Brain.
* **For all members**: This is a Workspace connection, which can only be enabled by a Workspace owner or admin. Everyone in the Workspace will be able to use tools from this connection in Super Agents and Brain.

# Admin controls for connections

# Connect an external MCP server

Before connecting, check with your MCP provider to identify which authentication method and headers they expect. Mirror these when connecting the server in ClickUp.

MCP servers must have a public URL to connect.

ClickUp does not use fixed outbound IP addresses for Brain and Super Agent connections to external MCP servers. Outbound traffic uses dynamically assigned cloud IP addresses, so IP allowlisting is not supported. Secure your MCP server endpoint using OAuth or API key authentication.

To connect an external MCP server to your Workspace:

1. Open the App Center:
   * In the upper-left corner, click your Workspace avatar and select **Apps**.
   * In your Global Navigation, click **More** and select **Apps**.
   * Use the **Open App Center** command in the AI Command Bar.
2. In the App Center sidebar, select **Custom MCP**.
3. Click Add New at the bottom or select one of the templates.
4. Choose the connection type:
   * **For all members** or **Workspace** tab: Set up a Workspace connection.
   * **Just for me** or **Personal** tab: Set up a personal connection.
5. Click **Next**.
6. Add your server information in the necessary fields or authorize your account if you're using one of our templates. For custom servers, you must include a name, URL, and authentication method. Optionally, you can add a server icon and description.

7. When connecting a custom MCP server, there are three authorization methods you can choose from:
   * **OAuth:** You'll be redirected to the provider's OAuth flow, then returned to ClickUp. Some providers require a redirect/callback URL to be registered before you can connect. Use https://search.clickup-prod.com/connect/mcp.
   * **API key:** Enter your API key. If your provider requires them, enter the custom headers. If valid, ClickUp will connect and display the available tools.
   * **No authentication:** Connect ClickUp directly. If your provider requires them, enter the custom headers. If valid, ClickUp will connect and display the available tools.
8. When connecting a custom MCP server, you can customize the Client ID, Client Secret, and Scopes in the **Advanced configuration** section.

9. Once connected, you'll see all of the available tools that you can now add to Super Agents and use in Brain listed in the app's **AI Tools** section.

## Use a MCP template

ClickUp offers templates so you can easily connect to some of the most popular MCP servers.

To connect an external MCP server using one of these templates:

1. Open the App Center:
   * In the upper-left corner, click your Workspace avatar and select **Apps**.
   * In your Global Navigation, click **More** and select **Apps**.
   * Use the **Open App Center** command in the AI Command Bar.
2. In the App Center sidebar, select **MCP Servers**.
3. Click the template you want to use.
4. By default, you'll be on the **Personal** tab. To set up a Workspace connection, click the **Workspace** tab.
5. Select **Connect**.
6. Complete the authorization steps to connect the external MCP server.

# Add MCP tools to Super Agents

Now that your MCP server is connected, its tools are available for use in your Super Agents.

Tool availability and behavior depend on the external MCP server provider.

## Add MCP tools to an existing Super Agent

To add tools from an MCP server you've connected to an existing Super Agent:

1. Open your Super Agent's profile.
2. In the **Tools** section, click **Add tools**.
3. Search for and select an MCP template, or click **Custom MCP Server** to add a custom one.
4. Add the MCP tools:
   * Add all of the MCP server's tools by clicking **Add all** at the top of the menu.
   * Add individual tools by selecting each one.

Don't forget to update the Super Agent's instructions as well!

## Add MCP tools when creating a Super Agent

If you mention a workflow involving an MCP server you've connected while building a Super Agent, the tools from that server are automatically added to the Super Agent after it is created.

# Workspace audit logs and MCP servers

Workspace audit logs include information about external MCP servers that were set up in the Workspace. Those with access to your Workspace audit logs can see the following information for external MCP servers:

* Who connected an external MCP server and the date and time it was done
* Who disconnected an external MCP server and the date and time it was done
* Who updated an external MCP server and the date and time it was done
* Whether the external MCP server connection is Workspace or personal
* The external MCP server details:
  + Name
  + Server URL
  + Authorization type
